newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Alliance outlines post-election stance.
newsitem.headline: NZ Alliance outlines post-election stance.

text.p: New Zealand Alliance leader Jim Anderton on Tuesday said the five party left-wing grouping would support votes of confidence to secure stable government after the general election.

But he said for the Alliance to suppport a minority government there would first have to be established an agreed programme and a process by which the Alliance could negotiate changes to government policy.
But Anderton said that was a powerful, not an impotent position as some commentators including former Labour Prime Minister David Lange had suggested.

He said discussions with other parties to secure support for a minority government should include the composition of select committees, questions in the House, access for private members' bills and the use of the finance minister's financial veto over measures which have a significant impact on the fiscal position.

On current polling the Alliance is drawing about 12 percent support, enough to give it the balance of power between the ruling National Party and a grouping of the two main opposition parties, Labour and New Zealand First, after the October 12 election.

Anderton ruled out any formal coalition deal after the election, saying that would require a breach of manifesto policy commitments. The other main parties have ruled out a negotiated position going into the election, leaving the Alliance effectively the only major party excluded from government-forming.

He again ruled out support for a National government but said the Alliance might support another party or parties on the basis of an agreed programme. He said its aim would be to "move policy towards what we and our constituency wants".
"If you have the numbers (to pass a vote of no-confidence) then you must be prepared to form an alternative government," Anderton said.
But he would not rule out voting down a centre-left minority government and possibly provoking another election if neither potential government advanced a programme the Alliance approved of.
"The only way a government can get our support is through an agreed programme with us," he said.
He said the Alliance would want to see a public joint policy position of Labour and New Zealand First before supporting such a government.
He again offered an invitation to other parties to negotiate an agreed position before the election.
Tentative discussions between Labour president Michael Hirschfeld and the Alliance leadership were scrapped earlier this year by Labour leader Helen Clark.
